improvement_directive: Replace the binary positive-Gram/no-Gram split with a strength-indexed class whose pre-period Gram may decay, and prove a matching minimax width frontier—including the transition to constant width and an adaptive attaining band or a matching adaptation impossibility. Derive the lower-pair feasibility from primitive model constants instead of assuming the witness-specific survival, density-floor, and Hölder conditions.
critique: The note proves a sharp rank-one width, only a higher-rank bracket with an unresolved estimator-specific eta_D term, and an order-one worst-case boundary for a class deliberately allowing the pre-period Gram to vanish. The latter transfers a genuine impossibility to the broader factor-and-span structure of the public Han–Shah Theorem 1 model, but it does not characterize the width as identification strength deteriorates or provide a usable boundary-adaptive procedure. Both converse constructions also depend on ass:explicit-witness-compatibility, a proof-tailored condition that already certifies most of the least-favorable curves' survival validity, density floor, smoothness, and numerical feasibility rather than deriving them from primitive class restrictions. The framing accurately describes the higher-rank result as a bracket and does not stale-claim unrestricted W_r^* asymptotic to rho_r, but the delivered collection remains a strong specialized inference result rather than a flagship resolution or broadly established framework.
